en: Title: *Mahāvairocanābhisambodhi* Fragment Source: Wang, Junqi. 2022. “A Preliminary Study of a Newly Discovered Sanskrit Manuscript of the *Mahāvairocanābhisambodhi*. *Journal of Indian and Buddhist Studies* 70/3: (64) 1102–(70) 1108.

"May the Master attend to me: I, named so-and-so, from this moment until I sit upon the seat of enlightenment, request that the Master grant me the vow of entry into the Great Samaya. I shall uphold it upon my head as the command of the Teacher."

Then the teacher should also say: "Pay attention, noble son, until you sit upon the seat of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*). You must offer yourself to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, desiring unexcelled, perfect enlightenment with a resolute intention (*adhyāśaya*)."

O Lord of Guhyakas, this is the vow called "The Entrance into the Great Samaya. Bodhisattvas who abide in this vow and practice the conduct of the bodhisattva through the gateway of mantra become those whose ethical discipline is well-restrained; they become established in the unsurpassed ethical discipline of the Tathāgatas. Therefore, O Lord of Guhyakas, a bodhisattva who wishes to train here in the gateway of the bodhisattva’s conduct through the gateway of mantra should apply himself to this entrance into the Great Samaya.

"Listen, Lord of Guhyakas, to that bodhicitta endowed with which bodhisattvas are born into the family of the Tathāgatas and become established in the wisdom of the Blessed Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
Then Vajrapāṇi said this to the Blessed One: "May the Blessed One, out of compassion for us, teach that bodhicitta."

When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of the Guhyakas: "In that regard, Lord of the Guhyakas, what is awakening (*bodhi*)? Awakening is space; and space is formless, invisible, and ungraspable. Whatever is the characteristic of awakening, such is the characteristic of the mind. For, Lord of the Guhyakas, the mind, space, and awakening—these are non-dual. That which is the realization of the equality of phenomena and the attainment of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) therein is unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening. The mind that arises therein through the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension—this, Lord of the Guhyakas, is called the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*)."

Moreover, Lord of Guhyakas, Bodhisattvas awaken to enlightenment through five points of abiding. What are these five? Here, Lord of Guhyakas, some Bodhisattvas awaken to that which is free from all entities (*sarvabhāvavigata*). Others, however, awaken to that which is empty, like an illusion, being free from the aggregates, elements, sense-fields, and the grasped and the grasper. Some awaken by way of taking phenomena as their objective support (*dharmālambanatayā*). Furthermore, Lord of Guhyakas, a Bodhisattva practicing the conduct of the Bodhisattva path through the gateway of mantra should awaken in this way: "My own mind is free from all entities, devoid of the aggregates, elements, sense-fields, and the grasped and the grasper; by virtue of the equality of the selflessness of phenomena (*dharmanairātmyasamatayā*), it is primordially unarisen and has emptiness as its intrinsic nature."

In this regard, Lord of Guhyakas, the Tathāgata has demonstrated that "being free from all entities" refers precisely to the abandonment of the mundane path. Furthermore, herein no self, sentient being, creature, or human person is found; rather, there are only the aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and sense-bases (*āyatana*). By means of the gateway of the thorough knowledge of the realization of the Śrāvaka path, the Mahāyāna realization of Bodhisattvas is established as being "free from the grasping at the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases. However, through the equality of the selflessness of phenomena (*dharmanairātmya*), those Bodhisattvas who practice the conduct of the Bodhisattva via the gateway of mantra perceive their own minds as primordially unarisen; they awaken to [the mind] as having emptiness as its intrinsic nature, being without substance, and without characteristics. Therefore, Lord of Guhyakas, a Bodhisattva should generate a mind that is free from the storehouse-consciousness (*ālaya*), free from obscurations, and devoid of all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*).

Therefore, by this very method it should also be understood: that for those bodhisattvas who have set out in the Mahāyāna, there is nothing to be known as an aid toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment except for the gateway of liberation consisting in the accomplishment of the system of mantra practice. Why is that? Because for many eons, bodhisattvas, though striving and exerting themselves and performing difficult acts of renunciation, do not awaken to enlightenment; yet here in this very life, bodhisattvas who practice the conduct of the bodhisattva through the gateway of mantras awaken to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Why is that? Lord of Guhyakas, "birth" is a designation made by the Tathāgata for arising. For those bodhisattvas, that designation has ceased from the very beginning, because they have attained the samādhi for the realization of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena.

Then the Blessed One Vairocana again addressed Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Guhyakas: "In this regard, O Lord of Guhyakas, a bodhisattva who wishes to enter the samaya of the Secret Essence Maṇḍala must avoid five things from afar. What are these five? Stinginess, malice toward sentient beings, doubt, laziness, and lack of respect for the mantras and so forth. These qualities, O Lord of Guhyakas, must be avoided from afar by bodhisattvas who wish to enter the supramundane path in this very life. O Lord of Guhyakas, I do not say that there is even the slightest fulfillment of the bodhisattva conduct for a bodhisattva who remains established in these qualities. Why is that?"
